clue.text: Fabric produced by males

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A cloth that is somehow manufactured by men.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'males' supplies two male animals in a row: BUCK and then RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding and to stiffen clothes.

clue.text: Buzzers keep boy early

indicators.note: the insects keep the boy, holding him inside

parts.note: bees are insects that buzz
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Insects detain a lad at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Betimes is an old word meaning early or in good time.

clue.text: Leer rudely at bosom — way of a place up north

parts.note: the bosom is the chest

indicators.note: the word is roughly handled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a street is a way or road

explanation.surface: A man ogles a woman's chest in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' rearranges LEER to ERLE. Chester-le-Street is a town in County Durham, north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester-le-Street is a market town in County Durham in the north of England.

clue.text: A lot of water for garden or one sprinkler

indicators.note: a sprinkler scatters, so the letters before it are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A large volume of water is needed for a garden, or one sprinkler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprinkler' is a noun used as the anagram signal, which makes it hard to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is a major river forming part of the US-Mexico border.

clue.text: Ben leaves Sussex town centre

indicators.note: the surname departs from the town's name

parts.note: Midhurst is a market town in West Sussex
Ben-Hur is the chariot-racing hero of the novel and film, so Ben brings his surname

explanation.surface: A man called Ben leaves a southern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' stands for Ben-Hur, so 'leaves' takes HUR out of MIDHURST, a West Sussex town.
explanation.definitionFit: The midst is the middle or central part of something.

clue.text: Order whose disorder is spread about by whatever means

indicators.note: the jumbled word is spread about, wrapping round the honour's letters
putting the word whose into disorder rearranges its letters

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A religious order whose chaos somehow becomes known to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges the letters to SEHOW; 'is spread about' wraps that round the honour. 'Order' reads like a command, but it is the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Somehow is an adverb meaning in some way or other, by any means available.

clue.text: Place for an office

explanation.surface: Somewhere to put a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a location or site, and also a post or job one holds.

clue.text: Cope without a dermal inflammation

indicators.note: the coping word goes without the letter, losing it

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Dealing with life without a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Mange is a skin disease of animals caused by mites, giving itching and hair loss.

clue.text: Youth starts in emotional trauma, but quickly gets sustenance

indicators.note: that letter goes into the emotional trauma

parts.note: heartbreak is overwhelming emotional distress

indicators.note: the start of the word youth gives its opening letter

parts.note: fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A heartbroken young person soon finds something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth starts' gives just Y, which 'in' tucks into the trauma word, giving HEARTYBREAK. 'quickly' looks like part of the surface but supplies the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty breakfast is a substantial morning meal, a source of nourishment for the day.

clue.text: Settle one new dog and duck

indicators.note: settling the letters puts them into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Resolve the matter of one new dog and a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an anagram signal but is fodder; 'Settle' rearranges I, NEW and DOG. The bird is more often spelt wigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A widgeon is a dabbling duck with a whistling call.

clue.text: The overhaul including former support for a fiscal device

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the turned-round haul word holds the next two pieces inside it

parts.note: read cheekily as over-haul: haul is drag, and over turns it round
old means former, as in an old flame
a stand is something that supports, as for a music score

explanation.surface: An overhaul of the system includes a support from earlier, all to regulate money.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius cheekily splits 'overhaul': haul is DRAG, and 'over' reads it backwards; 'including' puts the other two pieces inside that turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: The gold standard tied a currency's value to gold, a monetary rule rather than strictly a tax measure.

clue.text: Test or the object thereof

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A test, or else the thing being tested.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT (Ministry of Transport) test is the yearly British check that a car is roadworthy, and a car is the thing it examines.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor, British slang for a car, is what the MOT test examines.

clue.text: Wood with intent of brewing

parts.note: teak is a hard tropical timber
ettle is a Scots and northern dialect word for intent or purpose

explanation.surface: Timber used with the aim of making beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' suggests beer, but it is tea that is brewed in this pot. ETTLE is an old Scots word for intention.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea kettle is the vessel used to boil water for brewing tea, so it belongs to brewing.

clue.text: Green site building in Tanzania

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are being built into a new structure

explanation.surface: A green-field site is being developed in an East African country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is the great savannah plain of northern Tanzania, famous for its wildlife migrations.

clue.text: Walk along the seafront to please and refresh

indicators.note: to refresh the letters is to renew them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A seaside stroll pleases and revives you.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long open promenade, especially beside the sea.

clue.text: The majority of ministers have a modest abode

indicators.note: most of the word, with a couple of letters lost from its end

parts.note: the cabinet is the body of senior government ministers

explanation.surface: Most government ministers live in humble homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The majority of' drops the last two letters of CABINET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a small, simple dwelling such as a hut in the woods.

clue.text: Oddly, it's not straight to include monetary commitments

indicators.note: the curly word holds the debts inside it

parts.note: something curly is not straight
IOUs are written promises to pay money

explanation.surface: Strangely, a crooked deal includes promises to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Curiously means in a strange or unusual way, a synonym for oddly.

clue.text: Material rejected in the percentage return

indicators.note: return says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fabric that was turned down comes back as a share of the takings.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin fabric with a crinkled surface.

clue.text: Thin skin sounds the signal for a light touch

indicators.note: the two words are spoken, giving the same sound as the entry

parts.words: the signal for a light touch
parts.note: a cue is a signal and a tickle is a light touch, joined

explanation.surface: A thin membrane calls out for a gentle stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' signals that cue plus tickle, said together, give the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the thin layer of skin at the base of a fingernail.

clue.text: Corresponding member of society following reported pioneer

indicators.note: the pioneer's name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: William Penn founded the colony of Pennsylvania
a Friend is a member of the Religious Society of Friends, the Quakers

explanation.surface: A member of a club follows a much-talked-about trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts FRIEND after the sound of PENN. The definition is loose: the answer is someone you correspond with.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen friend is someone with whom you exchange letters, so it describes corresponding.

clue.text: Wobbly soft middle with cellulite

indicators.note: the wobbling letters shift into a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A wobbly, soft belly with orange-peel skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulite gives skin a lumpy, pitted look, so dimpled describes it.

clue.text: Buttons with evidence of right found in book

parts.note: title is the legal right of ownership or the document proving it
Buttons is the traditional name for a page boy, as in the pantomime Cinderella

explanation.surface: Clothes fasteners with proof of entitlement turn up in a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttons' is capitalised to hide the pantomime page boy, a British Christmas-show character.
explanation.definitionFit: A title page is the leaf at the front of a book giving its title and author.

clue.text: Letter for a girl to follow

parts.note: en is the spelt-out name of the letter N
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Correspondence sent for a young woman to pursue.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards, to follow as a result.

clue.text: Rue losing head over a bird

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Regretting the loss of a leader over a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron with long plumes.

clue.text: Interjection used with wood to keep out the drink

parts.note: oak is a familiar timber
um is a hesitant interjection

explanation.surface: An exclamation made with timber to bar alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is crossword slang for the sea, not alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre driven into ship seams to make them watertight against the sea.

clue.text: Function for team using skills with its stock-in-trade

parts.note: Chelsea is a London football club
arts are skills, as in the arts of persuasion
a football team's essential equipment is the ball

explanation.surface: A team's do uses its skills and the tools of its trade.
explanation.walkthrough: CHELSEA is a London football team; the Chelsea Arts Ball was a famous fancy-dress party run by the Chelsea Arts Club.
explanation.definitionFit: A function is a formal social event such as a ball or party.

clue.text: Former time soldiers were uncompromising

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: In days gone by, the troops were hard-liners.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme views are radical ones that admit no compromise or moderation.

clue.text: Model Destry foolishly agreed to meet

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car

indicators.note: doing it foolishly mixes up the letters of the name

explanation.surface: A model foolishly arranged a date with a man named Destry.
explanation.walkthrough: Destry is the hero of the Western Destry Rides Again.
explanation.definitionFit: To tryst is to make an appointment to meet, usually a lovers' rendezvous.
